canonical_name: Hoffman spectral bound for independent sets (repository theorem-family label)
literal_source_claim_en: A spectral upper bound for independent sets.
source_attribution: Alan Hoffman, 1970 (uncited catalog metadata; historically disputed for the independence-number ratio bound)
statement_blocker: The catalog gives only a spectral upper bound for independent sets. It omits the graph model, finiteness and nonemptiness, regularity, order and degree binders, adjacency-matrix coefficient field, eigenvalue ordering and least-eigenvalue witness, denominator/sign convention, independence number versus each independent set, equality clause, and weighted or irregular variants. Haemers 2021 states the familiar regular-graph ratio bound but explicitly reports that Hoffman did not publish it and identifies Hoffman's 1970 coloring paper as a wrong reference for this result. Selecting a proposition or accepting the catalog year without source review would invent or misattribute mathematics.
target_decision: retain a planned intake and require independently reviewed source and exact-statement selection before ordinary statement or proof execution
domain_and_universes: Open: an accepted statement must fix the finite vertex carrier and universes, simple-graph representation, finiteness and decidability data, real or other adjacency-matrix coefficients, natural versus real cardinality casts, and every typeclass assumption.
conclusion: Open: the repository does not choose the regular-graph ratio inequality, an inequality for each independent set, the independence-number form, an equality characterization, or a weighted, irregular, Laplacian, clique, or chromatic variant.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded at intake because no proposition is selected; empty, singleton, edgeless, disconnected, and complete graphs, denominator zero or sign, repeated least eigenvalues, and natural-to-real casts must be resolved from the admitted statement.

the division-free equivalent (k - lambda_min) * alpha(G) <= -n * lambda_min under an explicit sign condition
the corresponding bound for the cardinality of every independent finset
the equality consequence that every vertex outside an extremal independent set has a constant number of neighbors inside it
a weighted-adjacency-matrix extension with constant row and column sums
an arbitrary-graph or Laplacian Hoffman-type bound
degenerate_cases_to_resolve: empty, singleton, and edgeless finite simple graphs
zero degree, zero least eigenvalue, and zero or sign-unknown denominator
disconnected regular graphs and multiplicities of extreme eigenvalues
complete graphs and graphs with isolated vertices
natural independence number versus real-valued spectral expression and all casts
least eigenvalue as an ordered index versus a spectral-minimality predicate
maximum independent set versus every independent set and empty independent sets
excluded_substitutions: Hoffman's chromatic-number lower bound or THM-M-0891 Wilf theorem
Delsarte's strongly-regular clique/coclique bound or a Lovasz-theta, Cvetkovic-inertia, normalized-Laplacian, or arbitrary-graph extension
a theorem that assumes the desired ratio inequality, positive-semidefinite certificate, or extremal cardinality as input
one computed graph, floating-point eigenspectrum, numerical experiment, or unchecked certificate
generic independent-set, regularity, adjacency-matrix, Hermitian-spectrum, or positive-semidefinite APIs alone
the catalog's untrusted verified label, 1970 attribution, modern source lead, or API probe as proof credit
